Correct answer: C

C: At a separation of , the strong nuclear force is in its attractive range (approximately to ). Since the strong force is charge-independent, it acts as an attractive force between any two nucleons (protons or neutrons). The electrostatic force only acts between charged particles; therefore, it is repulsive between two protons and zero for any pair involving a neutron.
